---
title: "How rcs is tested"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A storage package must not lose or mix up data, also when a network fails
halfway through a write. This article describes how the tests of rcs check
that, and how to run them. The code below is not run here: it starts the
test suite, which takes from seconds to many minutes depending on the level.

Two rules hold throughout the suite:

- every algorithm is compared with a slow, independent reference;
- every operation on a store is followed by a check of the store's
  invariants.

All tests use simulated data from the `rcs_sim_*()` generators, and every
store is built in temporary folders that are removed afterwards. The tests
use testthat (third edition).

## Test levels

The suite has three levels, chosen by the environment variable
`RCS_TEST_LEVEL`. Each level adds tests to the one before.

| Level | What it runs | Default when |
|---|---|---|
| `cran` | Unit tests: no network, small data, a few seconds per file. | `RCS_TEST_LEVEL` is unset and the tests run on CRAN or under `R CMD check`. |
| `default` | Adds the integration suite on local folders and property tests of about 200 random cases each. | `RCS_TEST_LEVEL` is unset otherwise, e.g. under `devtools::test()`. |
| `full` | Adds property tests of up to 2,000 cases, the random-operation test, and the suite against a Google Cloud Storage bucket. | Never; set it. |

Run each level from the package folder:

```{r}
# default: the local integration suite and property tests
devtools::test()

# cran: unit tests only
withr::with_envvar(c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "cran"), devtools::test())

# full: everything, including the random-operation test
withr::with_envvar(c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "full"), devtools::test())

# one file
devtools::test(filter = "intersects")
```

Inside the tests, `skip_below_level("default")` or `skip_below_level("full")`
at the top of a test skips it below that level, and `property_cases()` gives
the number of random cases of a property test at the current level. Both
live in `tests/testthat/helper-levels.R`.

## Store invariants

After every step of every integration test, `expect_store_valid(st)`
(`tests/testthat/helper-invariants.R`) reads the catalogs of every
available location again and checks, for each:

1. every file the catalog names (current and history) exists, with the
   recorded size and MD5 checksum, and its Parquet footer holds the
   recorded number of rows;
2. every dataset's version equals the hash of its file rows, and its totals
   (files, rows, bytes) equal the sums of those rows;
3. a manifest exists for every version in the catalog and agrees with it,
   and no file is named by two datasets;
4. with history off, no file exists that the catalog does not name, apart
   from files left by an injected failure, which `store_prune()` must then
   remove;
5. every index table agrees with its dataset: every row identifier exists
   and every recorded main cell equals the row's `h3`;
6. every secondary copy of a dataset either equals the primary's or is
   reported as `missing` or `differs` by `store_status()`.

It also checks that the connection object holds the catalogs that are
stored, so that a function that changed a location updated the object in
place. All problems are collected and reported in one failure.

## Failures and crash points

A backend stub (`tests/testthat/helper-backend-stub.R`) wraps the local
backend, counts the calls made through it and, on chosen calls, fails or
silently alters a written file. With it the tests check, among others:

- a failure of the primary during upload, or between two catalog files:
  no catalog changes, and repeating the call succeeds and copies only what
  is missing;
- a failure of a secondary during a write: a warning, the secondary is
  reported as behind, and `store_sync()` repairs it;
- a transient error on the first two attempts of one file: the write
  succeeds;
- an upload that silently alters a file: the MD5 check stops the write;
- a catalog changed by another writer between the start of a write and its
  catalog switch: the write stops and changes nothing;
- a stale lock on a local location is taken over, a fresh one blocks.

The **crash-point matrix** goes through every backend call of an
operation. Each of `store_write()` (every mode), `store_sync()`,
`store_delete()` and `store_prune()` is first run with a counting stub to
learn its number of backend calls, N. It is then run N times, failing at
call 1, 2, ..., N, on the primary and on a secondary. After each failure
the invariants hold, readers see the old or the new version and never a
mixture, and repeating the call succeeds.

```{r}
stub <- local_backend_stub(uri = primary)
run_operation()
n <- stub$calls
for (k in seq_len(n)) {
  reset_fixture()
  stub_reset(stub)
  stub$fail_at <- k
  expect_error(run_operation(), class = "rcs_error_stub")
  stub$fail_at <- NULL
  expect_store_valid(st, orphans_ok = TRUE)
}
```

## The random-operation test

At level `full`, seeded sequences of 50 operations run against three local
locations and, in parallel, against a plain model in memory: a named list
of data frames per location. The operations are create, replace, update,
delete, sync, copy, prune, rebuild, an injected failure, and switching
history on or off for the store, the connection or one dataset. After every
step the invariants hold, and `store_read()` of every dataset from every
location equals the model. A failing run prints its seed and its list of
operations, so it can be replayed.

## Reference oracles

The algorithms of the package are checked against slow references that
share no code with it (`tests/testthat/helper-geo-reference.R` and the
tests themselves):

- the `h3` cell of every simulated row equals the cell of largest overlap
  found by brute force, by intersecting the geometry with every nearby cell
  on the sphere;
- the index table's rows equal the cells a brute-force intersection with
  the cell grid finds, for every row that crosses a cell edge;
- the cells computed for a query contain every cell that a dense grid of
  points finds, for random shapes including thin strips, large rectangles
  with four vertices, shapes with holes and single points;
- a spatial read returns exactly the rows of `sf::st_filter()` on the whole
  dataset, for random query shapes and H3 cells of resolutions 2 to 9, and
  a superset with `exact = FALSE`; repeated for a projected CRS, for
  partitioned and unpartitioned datasets, for `geocode = FALSE`, for points
  and lines, and with `sf::sf_use_s2()` on and off;
- the polygons across the antimeridian and around the pole get the
  brute-force cells, are found from either side of ±180° and at the pole,
  and are not returned by a query elsewhere;
- a round trip of every column type (logical, integer, double, text with
  non-ASCII characters, factors with unused levels, ordered factors, dates,
  times with time zones, time differences, 64-bit integers, list columns,
  missing values, zero rows, every geometry type) is `identical()` after
  normalisation, for one file and for partitioned datasets.

## Other checks

- **Detection:** an altered data file, a missing data file, a truncated
  catalog, a wrong MD5 in the catalog and a manifest that disagrees with
  the catalog are each caught by `store_check()`, with a message naming the
  file.
- **Determinism:** the same data written twice give the same version;
  changing one value changes it.
- **Work counters:** with `options(rcs.trace = TRUE)` the package counts
  backend calls, files opened, row groups and rows (see `rcs_trace()`).
  Because the counts are exact, tests assert them: listing and describing
  a store open no data file, a filter on partition columns opens only the
  matching files, a repeated identical write uploads no data file.
- **Messages:** every print method, write summary and error message is
  covered by a snapshot test (`expect_snapshot()`).

## The cloud suite

At level `full`, the integration tests also run against Google Cloud
Storage when the environment variable `RCS_TEST_GCS` names a bucket. Each
run works under a random prefix in that bucket and removes it at the end.
Use a dedicated, empty bucket, and set up credentials as described in
`vignette("locations")`:

```{r}
withr::with_envvar(
  c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "full", RCS_TEST_GCS = "gs://my-test-bucket"),
  devtools::test()
)
```

Without `RCS_TEST_GCS`, and on CRAN, these tests are skipped.

## Coverage

```{r}
covr::package_coverage()
```

The aim is at least 90% of lines overall and 80% in every file.
